name: Veeble
tagline: cPanel hosting with LiteSpeed and multi-region data centers, from India to the US
description: Veeble is a smaller cPanel hosting provider offering LiteSpeed-powered shared, reseller and VPS plans from data centers in the US, UK, Germany, the Netherlands and India.
about: Veeble Hosting is a web hosting company running cPanel-based shared, reseller and VPS hosting alongside Windows hosting and dedicated servers. It positions itself around owned and co-located Tier IV data center capacity in the United States, United Kingdom, Germany, the Netherlands and India, which makes it a notable option for site owners specifically targeting an Indian audience with low-latency hosting.

Its cPanel shared hosting comes in three tiers — LaunchPad, ScaleUP and ProMaster — built on LiteSpeed web servers with NVMe storage, free Let's Encrypt SSL, a bundled CDN, a drag-and-drop site builder and the Softaculous installer for one-click app deployment (WordPress and 400+ other apps). Plans scale from a single site with 20GB storage and 5 email accounts on LaunchPad up to unlimited sites, email and databases with SSH access on ProMaster.

Veeble advertises a 99.9% uptime SLA with financial compensation for downtime and a renewal price-lock promise — the rate at signup is the rate charged at renewal, which stands apart from hosts that raise renewal pricing sharply after an introductory term. It is a much smaller brand than the major hosting names, so public track record (reviews, longevity signals, and independent benchmarks) is thinner; verify current specifics directly with Veeble before committing to a longer term.
policies: Independent reviews cite a 14-day money-back guarantee on hosting plans, alongside flexible 1, 3, 6 and 12-month billing terms — confirm the exact refund window and any exclusions on Veeble's own terms page before purchasing, since this wasn't independently confirmed on Veeble's own site at the time of writing.

Pricing varies by region/currency (Veeble shows INR pricing for its India-facing site) and drops substantially on longer prepaid terms — treat any headline monthly rate as term-dependent rather than a flat price.
